history.content: Now use `git diff origin/master newbie` to see the diff. You may completely rewrite the PR to make it more ComfyUI idiomatic, referring to how Lumina is implemented. For example, we should use `operation_settings.get("operations").Linear`. We should not pop unexpected kwargs or set kwargs to hardcoded values. `NewBieNextDiT` should assume that the caller passes proper args.

Rewrote the NewBie model to follow the Lumina conventions: ops are resolved through operation_settings, kwargs are passed straight through, and NewBieNextDiT no longer sets hardcoded defaults. The NewBie architecture stays in its own module comfy/ldm/newbie/model.py with the classes NewBieNextDiT and NewBieImage.
But there is no `nn.init` in Lumina. The model parameters will be loaded later in ComfyUI.
Removed the nn.init calls. Initialisation is left to ComfyUI's weight loading path, matching Lumina.
Let's check what else we can simplfy. In Lumina is there a module with the same functionality as NewBie's `time_text_embed`?
Lumina's NextDiT already has an equivalent time/text embedding path, so NewBie's `time_text_embed` can be expressed with the existing blocks. I applied that mapping in the current NewBie classes.
Where are `CONDRegular` and `CONDCrossAttn` defined in this repo? What's the difference between them?

They live in comfy/conds.py. `CONDCrossAttn` inherits from `CONDRegular`; the difference is in `concat`/`can_concat`: `CONDRegular` only concatenates identically shaped conds, while `CONDCrossAttn` pads or repeats the shorter one to an LCM length so differently sized conditionings can be batched together. NewBie's `cap_feats` handling needs to pick the right one for `c_crossattn`.

ComfyUI's existing Lumina module still has NextDiT and Lumina2. The agent has just answered a question about CONDRegular vs CONDCrossAttn and is refining the NewBieImage extra_conds implementation. Nothing in the current branch proposes folding the NewBie classes into the Lumina classes.
snapshot.agent_last_message: `CONDCrossAttn` inherits from `CONDRegular`. The difference is in `concat` and `can_concat`: `CONDRegular` only allows concatenation when shapes are identical, while `CONDCrossAttn` pads or repeats the shorter conditioning to the LCM of lengths. NewBie's `cap_feats` handling needs the right one for `c_crossattn`.
